ar: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ الٓر تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
en: (1) Alif, Lām, Rā.[582] These are the verses of the clear Book.
enNotes: [582]- See footnote to 2:1.
tr: Alif lām rā, tilka āyātul-kitābil-mubīn

ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ قُرْءَٰنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
en: (2) Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’ān[583] that you might understand.
enNotes: [583]- i.e., revealed in the Arabic language.
tr: Innā anzalnāhu qurʾānan ʿarabiyyal laʿallakum taʿqilūn

ar: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْقَصَصِ بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ وَإِن كُنتَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلْغَٰفِلِينَ
en: (3) We relate to you, [O Muḥammad], the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur’ān although you were, before it, among the unaware.
tr: Naḥnu naquṣṣu ʿalayka aḥsanal-qaṣaṣi bimā awḥaynā ilayka hādhal-qurʾān, waʾin kunta min qablihī laminal-ghāfilīn

ar: إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِى سَٰجِدِينَ
en: (4) [Of these stories mention] when Joseph said to his father,[584] "O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."
enNotes: [584]- The prophet Jacob (upon whom be peace).
tr: Idh qāla yūsufu liʾabīhi yā abati innī raʾaytu aḥada ʿashara kawkabaw wash-shamsa wal-qamara raʾaytuhum lī sājidīn

ar: قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُءْيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا۟ لَكَ كَيْدًا إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ
en: (5) He said, "O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy.
tr: Qāla yābunayya lā taqṣuṣ ruʾyāka ʿalā ikhwatika fayakīdū laka kaydā, innash-shayṭāna lil-insāni ʿaduwwum mubīn

ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُۥ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
en: (6) And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives [i.e., events or dreams] and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise."
tr: Wakadhālika yajtabīka rabbuka wayuʿallimuka min taʾwīlil-aḥādīthi wayutimmu niʿmatahū ʿalayka waʿalā āli yaʿqūba kamā atammahā ʿalā abawayka min qablu ibrāhīma waʾisḥāq, inna rabbaka ʿalīmun ḥakīm

ar: لَّقَدْ كَانَ فِى يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِۦٓ ءَايَٰتٌ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
en: (7) Certainly were there in Joseph and his brothers signs for those who ask, [such as]
tr: Laqad kāna fī yūsufa waʾikhwatihī āyātul lis-sāʾilīn

ar: إِذْ قَالُوا۟ لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
en: (8) When they said, "Joseph and his brother[585] are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error.
enNotes: [585]- Benjamin, who was born of the same mother as Joseph.
tr: Idh qālū layūsufu waʾakhūhu aḥabbu ilā abīnā minnā wanaḥnu ʿuṣbah, inna abānā lafī ḍalālim mubīn

ar: ٱقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضًا يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ قَوْمًا صَٰلِحِينَ
en: (9) Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance [i.e., attention] of your father will [then] be only for you, and you will be after that a righteous people."[586]
enNotes: [586]- i.e., You can repent thereafter.
tr: Uqtulū yūsufa awiṭraḥūhu arḍay yakhlu lakum wajhu abīkum watakūnū mim baʿdihī qawman ṣāliḥīn

ar: قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ لَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ وَأَلْقُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ ٱلسَّيَّارَةِ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ
en: (10) Said a speaker among them, "Do not kill Joseph but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up - if you would do [something]."
tr: Qāla qāʾilum minhum lā taqtulū yūsufa waʾalqūhu fī ghayābatil-jubbi yaltaqiṭhu baʿḍus-sayyārati in kuntum fāʿilīn

ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لَا تَأْمَ۫نَّا عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَنَٰصِحُونَ
en: (11) They said, "O our father, why do you not entrust us with Joseph while indeed, we are to him sincere counselors?
tr: Qālū yā abānā mā laka lā taʾmannā ʿalā yūsufa waʾinnā lahū lanāṣiḥūn

ar: أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
en: (12) Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play. And indeed, we will be his guardians."
tr: Arsilhu maʿanā ghaday yartaʿ wayalʿab waʾinnā lahū laḥāfiẓūn

ar: قَالَ إِنِّى لَيَحْزُنُنِىٓ أَن تَذْهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَخَافُ أَن يَأْكُلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَأَنتُمْ عَنْهُ غَٰفِلُونَ
en: (13) [Jacob] said, "Indeed, it saddens me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware."
tr: Qāla innī layaḥzununī an tadhhabū bihī waʾakhāfu ay yaʾkulahudh-dhiʾbu waʾantum ʿanhu ghāfilūn

ar: قَالُوا۟ لَئِنْ أَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّآ إِذًا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
en: (14) They said, "If a wolf should eat him while we are a [strong] clan, indeed, we would then be losers."
tr: Qālū laʾin akalahudh-dhiʾbu wanaḥnu ʿuṣbatun innā idhal lakhāsirūn

ar: فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَن يَجْعَلُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُم بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
en: (15) So when they took him [out] and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well...[587] But We inspired to him, "You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [your identity]."
enNotes: [587]- The conclusion of this sentence is estimated to be "...they tormented him."
tr: Falammā dhahabū bihī waʾajmaʿū ay yajʿalūhu fī ghayābatil-jubb, waʾawḥaynā ilayhi latunabbiʾannahum biʾamrihim hādhā wahum lā yashʿurūn

ar: وَجَآءُوٓ أَبَاهُمْ عِشَآءً يَبْكُونَ
en: (16) And they came to their father at night, weeping.
tr: Wajāʾū abāhum ʿishāʾay yabkūn

ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ وَتَرَكْنَا يُوسُفَ عِندَ مَتَٰعِنَا فَأَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَٰدِقِينَ
en: (17) They said, "O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Joseph with our possessions, and a wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful."
tr: Qālū yā abānā innā dhahabnā nastabiqu wataraknā yūsufa ʿinda matāʿinā faʾakalahudh-dhiʾb, wamā anta bimuʾminil lanā walaw kunnā ṣādiqīn

ar: وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ
en: (18) And they brought upon his shirt false blood.[588] [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allāh is the one sought for help against that which you describe."
enNotes: [588]- They had stained Joseph's shirt with the blood of a lamb but had forgotten to tear it, thereby arousing their father's suspicion.
tr: Wajāʾū ʿalā qamīṣihī bidamin kadhib, qāla bal sawwalat lakum anfusukum amrā, faṣabrun jamīl, wallāhul-mustaʿānu ʿalā mā taṣifūn

ar: وَجَآءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَأَرْسَلُوا۟ وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَىٰ دَلْوَهُۥ قَالَ يَٰبُشْرَىٰ هَٰذَا غُلَٰمٌ وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَٰعَةً وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ
en: (19) And there came a company of travelers; then they sent their water drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, "Good news! Here is a boy." And they concealed him, [taking him] as merchandise;[589] and Allāh was Knowing of what they did.
enNotes: [589]- To be sold as a slave.
tr: Wajāʾat sayyāratun faʾarsalū wāridahum faʾadlā dalwah, qāla yābushrā hādhā ghulām, waʾasarrūhu biḍāʿah, wallāhu ʿalīmum bimā yaʿmalūn

ar: وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍۭ بَخْسٍ دَرَٰهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ وَكَانُوا۟ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلزَّٰهِدِينَ
en: (20) And they sold him for a reduced price - a few dirhams - and they were, concerning him, of those content with little.
tr: Washarawhu bithamanim bakhsin darāhima maʿdūdah, wakānū fīhi minaz-zāhidīn

ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى ٱشْتَرَىٰهُ مِن مِّصْرَ لِٱمْرَأَتِهِۦٓ أَكْرِمِى مَثْوَىٰهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُۥ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَٱللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرِهِۦ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: (21) And the one from Egypt[590] who bought him said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable. Perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son." And thus, We established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events [i.e., dreams]. And Allāh is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
enNotes: [590]- The minister in charge of supplies, whose title was al-ʿAzeez.
tr: Waqālal-ladhishtarāhu mim miṣra limraʾatihī akrimī mathwāhu ʿasā ay yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahū waladā, wakadhālika makkannā liyūsufa fil-arḍ, walinuʿallimahū min taʾwīlil-aḥādīth, wallāhu ghālibun ʿalā amrihī walākinna aktharan-nāsi lā yaʿlamūn

ar: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥٓ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: (22) And when he [i.e., Joseph] reached maturity, We gave him judgement and knowledge. And thus We reward the doers of good.
tr: Walammā balagha ashuddahū ātaynāhu ḥukmaw waʿilmā, wakadhālika najzil-muḥsinīn

ar: وَرَٰوَدَتْهُ ٱلَّتِى هُوَ فِى بَيْتِهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ وَغَلَّقَتِ ٱلْأَبْوَٰبَ وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُۥ رَبِّىٓ أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَاىَ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
en: (23) And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, "Come, you." He said, "[I seek] the refuge of Allāh. Indeed, he[591] is my master, who has made good my residence. Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed."
enNotes: [591]- Her husband, al-ʿAzeez.
tr: Warāwadathul-latī huwa fī baytihā ʿan nafsihī waghallaqatil-abwāba waqālat hayta lak, qāla maʿādhallāhi innahū rabbī aḥsana mathwāy, innahū lā yufliḥuẓ-ẓālimūn

ar: وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِۦ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَآ أَن رَّءَا بُرْهَٰنَ رَبِّهِۦ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
en: (24) And she certainly determined [to seduce] him, and he would have inclined to her had he not seen the proof [i.e., sign] of his Lord. And thus [it was] that We should avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.
tr: Walaqad hammat bihī wahamma bihā, lawlā ar raʾā burhāna rabbih, kadhālika linaṣrifa ʿanhus-sūʾa wal-faḥshāʾ, innahū min ʿibādinal-mukhlaṣīn

ar: وَٱسْتَبَقَا ٱلْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُۥ مِن دُبُرٍ وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَا ٱلْبَابِ قَالَتْ مَا جَزَآءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوٓءًا إِلَّآ أَن يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
en: (25) And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her husband at the door. She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"
tr: Wastabaqal-bāba waqaddat qamīṣahū min duburiw waʾalfayā sayyidahā ladal-bāb, qālat mā jazāʾu man arāda biʾahlika sūʾan illā ay yusjana aw ʿadhābun alīm

ar: قَالَ هِىَ رَٰوَدَتْنِى عَن نَّفْسِى وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ فَصَدَقَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
en: (26) [Joseph] said, "It was she who sought to seduce me." And a witness from her family testified, "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars.
tr: Qāla hiya rāwadatnī ʿan nafsī washahida shāhidum min ahlihā, in kāna qamīṣuhū qudda min qubulin faṣadaqat wahuwa minal-kādhibīn

ar: وَإِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
en: (27) But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful."
tr: Waʾin kāna qamīṣuhū qudda min duburin fakadhabat wahuwa minaṣ-ṣādiqīn

ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا قَمِيصَهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ مِن كَيْدِكُنَّ إِنَّ كَيْدَكُنَّ عَظِيمٌ
en: (28) So when he [i.e., her husband] saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, "Indeed, it is of your [i.e., women's] plan. Indeed, your plan is great [i.e., vehement].
tr: Falammā raʾā qamīṣahū qudda min duburin qāla innahū min kaydikunn, inna kaydakunna ʿaẓīm

ar: يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَٰذَا وَٱسْتَغْفِرِى لِذَنۢبِكِ إِنَّكِ كُنتِ مِنَ ٱلْخَاطِـِٔينَ
en: (29) Joseph, ignore this.[592] And, [my wife], ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinful."
enNotes: [592]- i.e., conceal it and act as if it had not taken place.
tr: Yūsufu aʿriḍ ʿan hādhā wastaghfirī lidhambik, innaki kunti minal-khāṭiʾīn

ar: وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ تُرَٰوِدُ فَتَىٰهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبًّا إِنَّا لَنَرَىٰهَا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
en: (30) And women in the city said, "The wife of al-ʿAzeez is seeking to seduce her slave boy; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her [to be] in clear error."
tr: Waqāla niswatun fil-madīnatimraʾatul-ʿazīzi turāwidu fatāhā ʿan nafsih, qad shaghafahā ḥubbā, innā lanarāhā fī ḍalālim mubīn

ar: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَـًٔا وَءَاتَتْ كُلَّ وَٰحِدَةٍ مِّنْهُنَّ سِكِّينًا وَقَالَتِ ٱخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُۥٓ أَكْبَرْنَهُۥ وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلْنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا هَٰذَا بَشَرًا إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ
en: (31) So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet and gave each one of them a knife and said [to Joseph], "Come out before them." And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands[593] and said, "Perfect is Allāh![594] This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel."
enNotes:
[593]- So distracted were they at the sight of him.
[594]- In His ability to create such beauty.
tr: Falammā samiʿat bimakrihinna arsalat ilayhinna waʾaʿtadat lahunna muttakaʾaw waʾātat kulla wāḥidatim minhunna sikkīnaw waqālatikhruj ʿalayhinn, falammā raʾaynahū akbarnahū waqaṭṭaʿna aydiyahunn, waqulna ḥāsha lillāhi mā hādhā basharā, in hādhā illā malakun karīm

ar: قَالَتْ فَذَٰلِكُنَّ ٱلَّذِى لُمْتُنَّنِى فِيهِ وَلَقَدْ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ فَٱسْتَعْصَمَ وَلَئِن لَّمْ يَفْعَلْ مَآ ءَامُرُهُۥ لَيُسْجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُونًا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
en: (32) She said, "That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused; and if he will not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be of those debased."
tr: Qālat fadhālikunnal-ladhī lumtunnanī fīh, walaqad rāwattuhū ʿan nafsihī fastaʿṣam, walaʾil lam yafʿal mā āmuruhū layusjananna walayakūnam minaṣ-ṣāghirīn

ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱلسِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِىٓ إِلَيْهِ وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّى كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
en: (33) He said, "My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant."
tr: Qāla rabbis-sijnu aḥabbu ilayya mimmā yadʿūnanī ilayh, waʾillā taṣrif ʿannī kaydahunna aṣbu ilayhinna waʾakum minal-jāhilīn

ar: فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
en: (34) So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
tr: Fastajāba lahū rabbuhū faṣarafa ʿanhu kaydahunn, innahū huwas-samīʿul-ʿalīm

ar: ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا۟ ٱلْـَٔايَٰتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُۥ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
en: (35) Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs[595] that he [i.e., al-ʿAzeez] should surely imprison him for a time.[596]
enNotes:
[595]- Proofs of his innocence.
[596]- Until the scandal be forgotten.
tr: Thumma badā lahum mim baʿdi mā raʾawul-āyāti layasjununnahū ḥattā ḥīn

ar: وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا وَقَالَ ٱلْـَٔاخَرُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِى خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦٓ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: (36) And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I have seen myself [in a dream] pressing [grapes for] wine." The other said, "Indeed, I have seen myself carrying upon my head [some] bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you to be of those who do good."
tr: Wadakhala maʿahus-sijna fatayān, qāla aḥaduhumā innī arānī aʿṣiru khamrā, waqālal-ākharu innī arānī aḥmilu fawqa raʾsī khubzan taʾkuluṭ-ṭayru minh, nabbiʾnā bitaʾwīlih, innā narāka minal-muḥsinīn

ar: قَالَ لَا يَأْتِيكُمَا طَعَامٌ تُرْزَقَانِهِۦٓ إِلَّا نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن يَأْتِيَكُمَا ذَٰلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِى رَبِّىٓ إِنِّى تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ قَوْمٍ لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَهُم بِٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ هُمْ كَٰفِرُونَ
en: (37) He said, "You will not receive food that is provided to you except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allāh, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
tr: Qāla lā yaʾtīkumā ṭaʿāmun turzaqānihī illā nabbaʾtukumā bitaʾwīlihī qabla ay yaʾtiyakumā, dhālikumā mimmā ʿallamanī rabbī, innī taraktu millata qawmil lā yuʾminūna billāhi wahum bil-ākhirati hum kāfirūn

ar: وَٱتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ ءَابَآءِىٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ مَا كَانَ لَنَآ أَن نُّشْرِكَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ ذَٰلِكَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ
en: (38) And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And it was not for us to associate anything with Allāh. That is from the favor of Allāh upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
tr: Wattabaʿtu millata ābāʾī ibrāhīma waʾisḥāqa wayaʿqūb, mā kāna lanā an nushrika billāhi min shayʾ, dhālika min faḍlillāhi ʿalaynā waʿalan-nāsi walākinna aktharan-nāsi lā yashkurūn

ar: يَٰصَٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ ءَأَرْبَابٌ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ
en: (39) O [my] two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allāh, the One,[597] the Prevailing?[598]
enNotes:
[597]- Single, individual and unique in His attributes and His deeds.
[598]- He who subdues doubts and false arguments with clear evidences and who subdues and imposes His will upon all creation.
tr: Yāṣāḥibayis-sijni aʾarbābum mutafarriqūna khayrun amillāhul-wāḥidul-qahhār

ar: مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَسْمَآءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَٰنٍ إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: (40) You worship not besides Him except [mere] names you have named them,[599] you and your fathers, for which Allāh has sent down no evidence. Legislation is not but for Allāh. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
enNotes: [599]- The false objects of worship which you have called "gods."
tr: Mā taʿbudūna min dūnihī illā asmāʾan sammaytumūhā antum waʾābāʾukum mā anzalallāhu bihā min sulṭān, inil-ḥukmu illā lillāh, amara allā taʿbudū illā iyyāh, dhālikad-dīnul-qayyimu walākinna aktharan-nāsi lā yaʿlamūn

ar: يَٰصَٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُۥ خَمْرًا وَأَمَّا ٱلْـَٔاخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِن رَّأْسِهِۦ قُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ
en: (41) O two companions of prison, as for one of you, he will give drink to his master of wine; but as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire."
tr: Yāṣāḥibayis-sijni ammā aḥadukumā fayasqī rabbahū khamrā, waʾammal-ākharu fayuṣlabu fataʾkuluṭ-ṭayru mir raʾsih, quḍiyal-amrul-ladhī fīhi tastaftiyān

ar: وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنسَىٰهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ
en: (42) And he said to the one whom he knew would go free, "Mention me before your master." But Satan made him forget the mention [to] his master, and he [i.e., Joseph] remained in prison several years.
tr: Waqāla lilladhī ẓanna annahū nājim minhumadhkurnī ʿinda rabbik, faʾansāhush-shayṭānu dhikra rabbihī falabitha fis-sijni biḍʿa sinīn

ar: وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِى فِى رُءْيَٰىَ إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ
en: (43) And [subsequently] the king said, "Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions."
tr: Waqālal-maliku innī arā sabʿa baqarātin simāniy yaʾkuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfuw wasabʿa sumbulātin khuḍriw waʾukhara yābisāt, yā ayyuhal-malaʾu aftūnī fī ruʾyāya in kuntum lir-ruʾyā taʿburūn

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَٰثُ أَحْلَٰمٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحْلَٰمِ بِعَٰلِمِينَ
en: (44) They said, "[It is but] a mixture of false dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams."
tr: Qālū aḍghāthu aḥlām, wamā naḥnu bitaʾwīlil-aḥlāmi biʿālimīn

ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا۠ أُنَبِّئُكُم بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦ فَأَرْسِلُونِ
en: (45) But the one who was freed and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth."
tr: Waqālal-ladhī najā minhumā waddakara baʿda ummatin ana unabbiʾukum bitaʾwīlihī faʾarsilūn

ar: يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِى سَبْعِ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
en: (46) [He said], "Joseph, O man of truth, explain to us about seven fat cows eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry - that I may return to the people [i.e., the king and his court]; perhaps they will know [about you]."
tr: Yūsufu ayyuhaṣ-ṣiddīqu aftinā fī sabʿi baqarātin simāniy yaʾkuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfuw wasabʿi sumbulātin khuḍriw waʾukhara yābisātil laʿallī arjiʿu ilan-nāsi laʿallahum yaʿlamūn

ar: قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدتُّمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ
en: (47) [Joseph] said, "You will plant for seven years consecutively; and what you harvest leave in its spikes, except a little from which you will eat.
tr: Qāla tazraʿūna sabʿa sinīna daʾabā, famā ḥaṣattum fadharūhu fī sumbulihī illā qalīlam mimmā taʾkulūn

ar: ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ
en: (48) Then will come after that seven difficult [years] which will consume what you advanced [i.e., saved] for them, except a little from which you will store.
tr: Thumma yaʾtī mim baʿdi dhālika sabʿun shidāduy yaʾkulna mā qaddamtum lahunna illā qalīlam mimmā tuḥṣinūn

ar: ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَامٌ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ
en: (49) Then will come after that a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press [olives and grapes]."
tr: Thumma yaʾtī mim baʿdi dhālika ʿāmun fīhi yughāthun-nāsu wafīhi yaʿṣirūn

ar: وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِى بِهِۦ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُ ٱلرَّسُولُ قَالَ ٱرْجِعْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَسْـَٔلْهُ مَا بَالُ ٱلنِّسْوَةِ ٱلَّٰتِى قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ إِنَّ رَبِّى بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٌ
en: (50) And the king said, "Bring him to me." But when the messenger came to him, [Joseph] said, "Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plan."
tr: Waqālal-malikuʾtūnī bih, falammā jāʾahur-rasūlu qālarjiʿ ilā rabbika fasʾalhu mā bālun-niswatillātī qaṭṭaʿna aydiyahunn, inna rabbī bikaydihinna ʿalīm

ar: قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَٰوَدتُّنَّ يُوسُفَ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ قُلْنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوٓءٍ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْـَٰٔنَ حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَنَا۠ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
en: (51) Said [the king to the women], "What was your condition when you sought to seduce Joseph?" They said, "Perfect is Allāh![600] We know about him no evil." The wife of al-ʿAzeez said, "Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful.
enNotes: [600]- In His ability to create such purity of character.
tr: Qāla mā khaṭbukunna idh rāwattunna yūsufa ʿan nafsih, qulna ḥāsha lillāhi mā ʿalimnā ʿalayhi min sūʾ, qālatimraʾatul-ʿazīzil-āna ḥaṣḥaṣal-ḥaqq, ana rāwattuhū ʿan nafsihī waʾinnahū laminaṣ-ṣādiqīn

ar: ذَٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّى لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى كَيْدَ ٱلْخَآئِنِينَ
en: (52) That is so he [i.e., al-ʿAzeez] will know that I did not betray him in [his] absence and that Allāh does not guide the plan of betrayers.
tr: Dhālika liyaʿlama annī lam akhunhu bil-ghaybi waʾannallāha lā yahdī kaydal-khāʾinīn

ar: وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِىٓ إِنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌۢ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّىٓ إِنَّ رَبِّى غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
en: (53) And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."[601]
enNotes: [601]- Although Ibn Katheer attributes the words of verses 52-53 to the wife of al-ʿAzeez, others have concluded that they were spoken by Joseph, thereby justifying his request for an inquiry and acknowledging Allāh's mercy to him.
tr: Wamā ubarriʾu nafsī, innan-nafsa laʾammāratum bis-sūʾi illā mā raḥima rabbī, inna rabbī ghafūrur raḥīm

ar: وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِى بِهِۦٓ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِى فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُۥ قَالَ إِنَّكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ
en: (54) And the king said, "Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively for myself." And when he spoke to him, he said, "Indeed, you are today established [in position] and trusted."
tr: Waqālal-malikuʾtūnī bihī astakhliṣhu linafsī, falammā kallamahū qāla innakal-yawma ladaynā makīnun amīn

ar: قَالَ ٱجْعَلْنِى عَلَىٰ خَزَآئِنِ ٱلْأَرْضِ إِنِّى حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ
en: (55) [Joseph] said, "Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian."
tr: Qālajʿalnī ʿalā khazāʾinil-arḍ, innī ḥafīẓun ʿalīm

ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَآءُ نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَن نَّشَآءُ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: (56) And thus We established Joseph in the land to settle therein wherever he willed. We touch with Our mercy whom We will, and We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
tr: Wakadhālika makkannā liyūsufa fil-arḍi yatabawwaʾu minhā ḥaythu yashāʾ, nuṣību biraḥmatinā man nashāʾu walā nuḍīʿu ajral-muḥsinīn

ar: وَلَأَجْرُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ يَتَّقُونَ
en: (57) And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were fearing Allāh.
tr: Walaʾajrul-ākhirati khayrul lilladhīna āmanū wakānū yattaqūn

ar: وَجَآءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَعَرَفَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ
en: (58) And the brothers of Joseph came [seeking food], and they entered upon him; and he recognized them, but he was to them unknown.[602]
enNotes: [602]- Due to the change in his appearance over the years.
tr: Wajāʾa ikhwatu yūsufa fadakhalū ʿalayhi faʿarafahum wahum lahū munkirūn

ar: وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمْ قَالَ ٱئْتُونِى بِأَخٍ لَّكُم مِّنْ أَبِيكُمْ أَلَا تَرَوْنَ أَنِّىٓ أُوفِى ٱلْكَيْلَ وَأَنَا۠ خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنزِلِينَ
en: (59) And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said, "Bring me a brother of yours from your father.[603] Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of accommodators?
enNotes: [603]- i.e., Benjamin, who had been kept at home by his father Jacob.
tr: Walammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim qālaʾtūnī biʾakhil lakum min abīkum, alā tarawna annī ūfil-kayla waʾana khayrul-munzilīn

ar: فَإِن لَّمْ تَأْتُونِى بِهِۦ فَلَا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِندِى وَلَا تَقْرَبُونِ
en: (60) But if you do not bring him to me, no measure will there be [hereafter] for you from me, nor will you approach me."
tr: Faʾil lam taʾtūnī bihī falā kayla lakum ʿindī walā taqrabūn

ar: قَالُوا۟ سَنُرَٰوِدُ عَنْهُ أَبَاهُ وَإِنَّا لَفَٰعِلُونَ
en: (61) They said, "We will attempt to dissuade his father from [keeping] him, and indeed, we will do [it]."
tr: Qālū sanurāwidu ʿanhu abāhu waʾinnā lafāʿilūn

ar: وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَٰنِهِ ٱجْعَلُوا۟ بِضَٰعَتَهُمْ فِى رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَآ إِذَا ٱنقَلَبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
en: (62) And [Joseph] said to his servants, "Put their merchandise[604] into their saddlebags so they might recognize it when they have gone back to their people that perhaps they will [again] return."
enNotes: [604]- The goods which they had brought to trade for food supplies.
tr: Waqāla lifityānihijʿalū biḍāʿatahum fī riḥālihim laʿallahum yaʿrifūnahā idhanqalabū ilā ahlihim laʿallahum yarjiʿūn

ar: فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيهِمْ قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا ٱلْكَيْلُ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَآ أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
en: (63) So when they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, [further] measure has been denied to us, so send with us our brother [that] we will be given measure. And indeed, we will be his guardians."
tr: Falammā rajaʿū ilā abīhim qālū yā abānā muniʿa minnal-kaylu faʾarsil maʿanā akhānā naktal waʾinnā lahū laḥāfiẓūn

ar: قَالَ هَلْ ءَامَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَآ أَمِنتُكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَخِيهِ مِن قَبْلُ فَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَٰفِظًا وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
en: (64) He said, "Should I entrust you with him except [under coercion] as I entrusted you with his brother before? But Allāh is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."
tr: Qāla hal āmanukum ʿalayhi illā kamā amintukum ʿalā akhīhi min qabl, fallāhu khayrun ḥāfiẓaw wahuwa arḥamur-rāḥimīn

ar: وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا۟ مَتَٰعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا۟ بِضَٰعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِى هَٰذِهِۦ بِضَٰعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ذَٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ
en: (65) And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies [i.e., food] for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."[605]
enNotes: [605]- For them. Or one obtained by us with ease.
tr: Walammā fataḥū matāʿahum wajadū biḍāʿatahum ruddat ilayhim, qālū yā abānā mā nabghī, hādhihī biḍāʿatunā ruddat ilaynā wanamīru ahlanā wanaḥfaẓu akhānā wanazdādu kayla baʿīr, dhālika kayluy yasīr

ar: قَالَ لَنْ أُرْسِلَهُۥ مَعَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لَتَأْتُنَّنِى بِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ فَلَمَّآ ءَاتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ
en: (66) [Jacob] said, "Never will I send him with you until you give me a promise [i.e., oath] by Allāh that you will bring him [back] to me, unless you should be surrounded [i.e., overcome by enemies]." And when they had given their promise, he said, "Allāh, over what we say, is Entrusted."[606]
enNotes: [606]- i.e., sufficient to witness and deal with the matter.
tr: Qāla lan ursilahū maʿakum ḥattā tuʾtūni mawthiqam minallāhi lataʾtunnanī bihī illā ay yuḥāṭa bikum, falammā ātawhu mawthiqahum qālallāhu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīl

ar: وَقَالَ يَٰبَنِىَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ مِنۢ بَابٍ وَٰحِدٍ وَٱدْخُلُوا۟ مِنْ أَبْوَٰبٍ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٍ وَمَآ أُغْنِى عَنكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ
en: (67) And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allāh at all. The decision is only for Allāh; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who would rely [indeed] rely."
tr: Waqāla yābaniyya lā tadkhulū mim bābiw wāḥidiw wadkhulū min abwābim mutafarriqah, wamā ughnī ʿankum minallāhi min shayʾ, inil-ḥukmu illā lillāh, ʿalayhi tawakkaltu waʿalayhi falyatawakkalil-mutawakkilūn

ar: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُم مَّا كَانَ يُغْنِى عَنْهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِى نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَىٰهَا وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِّمَا عَلَّمْنَٰهُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: (68) And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allāh at all except [it was] a need [i.e., concern] within the soul of Jacob, which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
tr: Walammā dakhalū min ḥaythu amarahum abūhum, mā kāna yughnī ʿanhum minallāhi min shayʾin illā ḥājatan fī nafsi yaʿqūba qaḍāhā, waʾinnahū ladhū ʿilmil limā ʿallamnāhu walākinna aktharan-nāsi lā yaʿlamūn

ar: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَنَا۠ أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
en: (69) And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself; he said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do [to me]."
tr: Walammā dakhalū ʿalā yūsufa āwā ilayhi akhāhu qāla innī ana akhūka falā tabtaʾis bimā kānū yaʿmalūn

ar: فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِى رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا ٱلْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَٰرِقُونَ
en: (70) So when he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the [gold measuring] bowl into the bag of his brother. Then an announcer called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves."
tr: Falammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim jaʿalas-siqāyata fī raḥli akhīhi thumma adhdhana muʾadhdhinun ayyatuhal-ʿīru innakum lasāriqūn

ar: قَالُوا۟ وَأَقْبَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِم مَّاذَا تَفْقِدُونَ
en: (71) They said while approaching them, "What is it you are missing?"
tr: Qālū waʾaqbalū ʿalayhim mādhā tafqidūn

ar: قَالُوا۟ نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ ٱلْمَلِكِ وَلِمَن جَآءَ بِهِۦ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا۠ بِهِۦ زَعِيمٌ
en: (72) They said, "We are missing the measure of the king. And for he who produces it is [the reward of] a camel's load, and I am responsible for it."
tr: Qālū nafqidu ṣuwāʿal-maliki waliman jāʾa bihī ḥimlu baʿīriw waʾana bihī zaʿīm

ar: قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُم مَّا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَٰرِقِينَ
en: (73) They said, "By Allāh, you have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we have not been thieves."
tr: Qālū tallāhi laqad ʿalimtum mā jiʾnā linufsida fil-arḍi wamā kunnā sāriqīn

ar: قَالُوا۟ فَمَا جَزَٰٓؤُهُۥٓ إِن كُنتُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ
en: (74) They [the accusers] said, "Then what would be its recompense[607] if you should be liars?"
enNotes: [607]- The punishment for theft.
tr: Qālū famā jazāʾuhū in kuntum kādhibīn

ar: قَالُوا۟ جَزَٰٓؤُهُۥ مَن وُجِدَ فِى رَحْلِهِۦ فَهُوَ جَزَٰٓؤُهُۥ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
en: (75) [The brothers] said, "Its recompense is that he in whose bag it is found - he [himself] will be its recompense.[608] Thus do we recompense the wrongdoers."
enNotes: [608]- According to their law, a convicted thief was made a slave of the one from whom he had stolen.
tr: Qālū jazāʾuhū maw wujida fī raḥlihī fahuwa jazāʾuh, kadhālika najziẓ-ẓālimīn

ar: فَبَدَأَ بِأَوْعِيَتِهِمْ قَبْلَ وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَخْرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ كَذَٰلِكَ كِدْنَا لِيُوسُفَ مَا كَانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِى دِينِ ٱلْمَلِكِ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَٰتٍ مَّن نَّشَآءُ وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِى عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ
en: (76) So he began [the search] with their bags before the bag of his brother; then he extracted it from the bag of his brother. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the religion [i.e., law] of the king except that Allāh willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, but over every possessor of knowledge is one [more] knowing.[609]
enNotes: [609]- Ending with the ultimate knowledge of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).
tr: Fabadaʾa biʾawʿiyatihim qabla wiʿāʾi akhīhi thummastakhrajahā miw wiʿāʾi akhīh, kadhālika kidnā liyūsuf, mā kāna liyaʾkhudha akhāhu fī dīnil-maliki illā ay yashāʾallāh, narfaʿu darajātim man nashāʾ, wafawqa kulli dhī ʿilmin ʿalīm

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِن يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِى نَفْسِهِۦ وَلَمْ يُبْدِهَا لَهُمْ قَالَ أَنتُمْ شَرٌّ مَّكَانًا وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَصِفُونَ
en: (77) They said, "If he steals - a brother of his has stolen before." But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them.[610] He said, "You are worse in position, and Allāh is most knowing of what you describe."
enNotes: [610]- He did not answer that he himself had been stolen by them from his father.
tr: Qālū iy yasriq faqad saraqa akhul lahū min qabl, faʾasarrahā yūsufu fī nafsihī walam yubdihā lahum, qāla antum sharrum makānā, wallāhu aʿlamu bimā taṣifūn

ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ إِنَّ لَهُۥٓ أَبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُۥٓ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: (78) They said, "O ʿAzeez,[611] indeed he has a father [who is] an old man, so take one of us in place of him. Indeed, we see you as a doer of good."
enNotes: [611]- Addressing Joseph, who now held the title of "al-ʿAzeez."
tr: Qālū yā ayyuhal-ʿazīzu inna lahū aban shaykhan kabīran fakhudh aḥadanā makānah, innā narāka minal-muḥsinīn

ar: قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ أَن نَّأْخُذَ إِلَّا مَن وَجَدْنَا مَتَٰعَنَا عِندَهُۥٓ إِنَّآ إِذًا لَّظَٰلِمُونَ
en: (79) He said, "[I seek] the refuge of Allāh [to prevent] that we take except him with whom we found our possession. Indeed, we would then be unjust."
tr: Qāla maʿādhallāhi an naʾkhudha illā maw wajadnā matāʿanā ʿindahū innā idhal laẓālimūn

ar: فَلَمَّا ٱسْتَيْـَٔسُوا۟ مِنْهُ خَلَصُوا۟ نَجِيًّا قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ عَلَيْكُم مَّوْثِقًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ مَا فَرَّطتُمْ فِى يُوسُفَ فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ ٱلْأَرْضَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْذَنَ لِىٓ أَبِىٓ أَوْ يَحْكُمَ ٱللَّهُ لِى وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ
en: (80) So when they had despaired of him, they secluded themselves in private consultation. The eldest of them said, "Do you not know that your father has taken upon you an oath by Allāh and [that] before you failed in [your duty to] Joseph? So I will never leave [this] land until my father permits me or Allāh decides for me,[612] and He is the best of judges.
enNotes: [612]- i.e., in my favor by bringing about the release of Benjamin.
tr: Falammastayʾasū minhu khalaṣū najiyyā, qāla kabīruhum alam taʿlamū anna abākum qad akhadha ʿalaykum mawthiqam minallāhi wamin qablu mā farraṭtum fī yūsufa falan abraḥal-arḍa ḥattā yaʾdhana lī abī aw yaḥkumallāhu lī, wahuwa khayrul-ḥākimīn

ar: ٱرْجِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيكُمْ فَقُولُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّ ٱبْنَكَ سَرَقَ وَمَا شَهِدْنَآ إِلَّا بِمَا عَلِمْنَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِلْغَيْبِ حَٰفِظِينَ
en: (81) Return to your father and say, 'O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew. And we were not witnesses of the unseen.[613]
enNotes: [613]- i.e., We could not have known when we gave you the oath that he would steal and be apprehended.
tr: Irjiʿū ilā abīkum faqūlū yā abānā innabnaka saraq, wamā shahidnā illā bimā ʿalimnā wamā kunnā lil-ghaybi ḥāfiẓīn

ar: وَسْـَٔلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ ٱلَّتِى كُنَّا فِيهَا وَٱلْعِيرَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَقْبَلْنَا فِيهَا وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ
en: (82) And ask the city in which we were and the caravan in which we came - and indeed, we are truthful.'"
tr: Wasʾalil-qaryatal-latī kunnā fīhā wal-ʿīral-latī aqbalnā fīhā, waʾinnā laṣādiqūn

ar: قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأْتِيَنِى بِهِمْ جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
en: (83) [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allāh will bring them to me all together. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."
tr: Qāla bal sawwalat lakum anfusukum amrā, faṣabrun jamīl, ʿasallāhu ay yaʾtiyanī bihim jamīʿā, innahū huwal-ʿalīmul-ḥakīm

ar: وَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنْهُمْ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَسَفَىٰ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَٱبْيَضَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ
en: (84) And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow over Joseph," and his eyes became white[614] from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor.[615]
enNotes:
[614]- i.e., he lost his sight.
[615]- He did not express the extent of his grief or his anger at what he suspected his sons had done but was patient, depending only upon Allāh for help.
tr: Watawallā ʿanhum waqāla yā asafā ʿalā yūsufa wabyaḍḍat ʿaynāhu minal-ḥuzni fahuwa kaẓīm

ar: قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ تَفْتَؤُا۟ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّىٰ تَكُونَ حَرَضًا أَوْ تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْهَٰلِكِينَ
en: (85) They said, "By Allāh, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become fatally ill or become of those who perish."
tr: Qālū tallāhi taftaʾu tadhkuru yūsufa ḥattā takūna ḥaraḍan aw takūna minal-hālikīn

ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشْكُوا۟ بَثِّى وَحُزْنِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
en: (86) He said, "I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allāh, and I know from Allāh that which you do not know.
tr: Qāla innamā ashkū baththī waḥuznī ilallāhi waʾaʿlamu minallāhi mā lā taʿlamūn

ar: يَٰبَنِىَّ ٱذْهَبُوا۟ فَتَحَسَّسُوا۟ مِن يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَا۟يْـَٔسُوا۟ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَا۟يْـَٔسُ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ
en: (87) O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allāh. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allāh except the disbelieving people."
tr: Yābaniyyadhhabū fataḥassasū miy yūsufa waʾakhīhi walā tayʾasū mir rawḥillāh, innahū lā yayʾasu mir rawḥillāhi illal-qawmul-kāfirūn

ar: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهْلَنَا ٱلضُّرُّ وَجِئْنَا بِبِضَٰعَةٍ مُّزْجَىٰةٍ فَأَوْفِ لَنَا ٱلْكَيْلَ وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنَآ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَجْزِى ٱلْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ
en: (88) So when they entered upon him [i.e., Joseph], they said, "O ʿAzeez, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with goods poor in quality, but give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allāh rewards the charitable."
tr: Falammā dakhalū ʿalayhi qālū yā ayyuhal-ʿazīzu massanā waʾahlanaḍ-ḍurru wajiʾnā bibiḍāʿatim muzjātin faʾawfi lanal-kayla wataṣaddaq ʿalaynā, innallāha yajzil-mutaṣaddiqīn

ar: قَالَ هَلْ عَلِمْتُم مَّا فَعَلْتُم بِيُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ إِذْ أَنتُمْ جَٰهِلُونَ
en: (89) He said, "Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"
tr: Qāla hal ʿalimtum mā faʿaltum biyūsufa waʾakhīhi idh antum jāhilūn

ar: قَالُوٓا۟ أَءِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ يُوسُفُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ يُوسُفُ وَهَٰذَآ أَخِى قَدْ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَآ إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
en: (90) They said, "Are you indeed Joseph?" He said, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allāh has certainly favored us. Indeed, he who fears Allāh and is patient, then indeed, Allāh does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good."
tr: Qālū aʾinnaka laʾanta yūsuf, qāla ana yūsufu wahādhā akhī qad mannallāhu ʿalaynā, innahū may yattaqi wayaṣbir faʾinnallāha lā yuḍīʿu ajral-muḥsinīn

ar: قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدْ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَٰطِـِٔينَ
en: (91) They said, "By Allāh, certainly has Allāh preferred you over us, and indeed, we have been sinners."
tr: Qālū tallāhi laqad ātharakallāhu ʿalaynā waʾin kunnā lakhāṭiʾīn

ar: قَالَ لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ يَغْفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
en: (92) He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. May Allāh forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful.
tr: Qāla lā tathrība ʿalaykumul-yawm, yaghfirullāhu lakum, wahuwa arḥamur-rāḥimīn

ar: ٱذْهَبُوا۟ بِقَمِيصِى هَٰذَا فَأَلْقُوهُ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِ أَبِى يَأْتِ بَصِيرًا وَأْتُونِى بِأَهْلِكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
en: (93) Take this, my shirt, and cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing. And bring me your family, all together."
tr: Idhhabū biqamīṣī hādhā faʾalqūhu ʿalā wajhi abī yaʾti baṣīrā, waʾtūnī biʾahlikum ajmaʿīn

ar: وَلَمَّا فَصَلَتِ ٱلْعِيرُ قَالَ أَبُوهُمْ إِنِّى لَأَجِدُ رِيحَ يُوسُفَ لَوْلَآ أَن تُفَنِّدُونِ
en: (94) And when the caravan departed [from Egypt], their father said,[616] "Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph [and would say that he was alive] if you did not think me weakened in mind."
enNotes: [616]- To those present with him, either some of his sons or other relatives.
tr: Walammā faṣalatil-ʿīru qāla abūhum innī laʾajidu rīḥa yūsufa lawlā an tufannidūn

ar: قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ إِنَّكَ لَفِى ضَلَٰلِكَ ٱلْقَدِيمِ
en: (95) They said, "By Allāh, indeed you are in your [same] old error."
tr: Qālū tallāhi innaka lafī ḍalālikal-qadīm

ar: فَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَ ٱلْبَشِيرُ أَلْقَىٰهُ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِۦ فَٱرْتَدَّ بَصِيرًا قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
en: (96) And when the bearer of good tidings[617] arrived, he cast it over his face, and he returned [once again] seeing. He said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allāh that which you do not know?"
enNotes: [617]- He who carried Joseph's shirt from among the brothers.
tr: Falammā an jāʾal-bashīru alqāhu ʿalā wajhihī fartadda baṣīrā, qāla alam aqul lakum innī aʿlamu minallāhi mā lā taʿlamūn

ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا ٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا خَٰطِـِٔينَ
en: (97) They said, "O our father, ask for us forgiveness of our sins; indeed, we have been sinners."
tr: Qālū yā abānastaghfir lanā dhunūbanā innā kunnā khāṭiʾīn

ar: قَالَ سَوْفَ أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكُمْ رَبِّىٓ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
en: (98) He said, "I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
tr: Qāla sawfa astaghfiru lakum rabbī, innahū huwal-ghafūrur-raḥīm

ar: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَبَوَيْهِ وَقَالَ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ مِصْرَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ءَامِنِينَ
en: (99) And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself [i.e., embraced them] and said, "Enter Egypt, Allāh willing, safe [and secure]."
tr: Falammā dakhalū ʿalā yūsufa āwā ilayhi abawayhi waqāladkhulū miṣra in shāʾallāhu āminīn

ar: وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ وَخَرُّوا۟ لَهُۥ سُجَّدًا وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ هَٰذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُءْيَٰىَ مِن قَبْلُ قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّى حَقًّا وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِىٓ إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِى مِنَ ٱلسِّجْنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْبَدْوِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِىٓ إِنَّ رَبِّى لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَآءُ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
en: (100) And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration.[618] And he said, "O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle[619] in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.
enNotes:
[618]- That of greeting and respect, which was lawful until the time of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ). Prostration to any person or object other than Allāh was then prohibited conclusively.
[619]- Perceptive of unapparent matters within which is benefit to His servants.
tr: Warafaʿa abawayhi ʿalal-ʿarshi wakharrū lahū sujjadā, waqāla yā abati hādhā taʾwīlu ruʾyāya min qabl, qad jaʿalahā rabbī ḥaqqā, waqad aḥsana bī idh akhrajanī minas-sijni wajāʾa bikum minal-badwi mim baʿdi an nazaghash-shayṭānu baynī wabayna ikhwatī, inna rabbī laṭīful limā yashāʾ, innahū huwal-ʿalīmul-ḥakīm

ar: رَبِّ قَدْ ءَاتَيْتَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِى مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ فَاطِرَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ أَنتَ وَلِىِّۦ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ تَوَفَّنِى مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
en: (101) My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous."
tr: Rabbi qad ātaytanī minal-mulki waʿallamtanī min taʾwīlil-aḥādīth, fāṭiras-samāwāti wal-arḍ, anta waliyyī fid-dunyā wal-ākhirah, tawaffanī muslimaw waʾalḥiqnī biṣ-ṣāliḥīn

ar: ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ أَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَمْكُرُونَ
en: (102) That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal, [O Muḥammad], to you. And you were not with them when they put together their plan while they conspired.
tr: Dhālika min ambāʾil-ghaybi nūḥīhi ilayk, wamā kunta ladayhim idh ajmaʿū amrahum wahum yamkurūn

ar: وَمَآ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
en: (103) And most of the people, although you strive [for it], are not believers.
tr: Wamā aktharun-nāsi walaw ḥaraṣta bimuʾminīn

ar: وَمَا تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
en: (104) And you do not ask of them for it any payment. It is not except a reminder to the worlds.
tr: Wamā tasʾaluhum ʿalayhi min ajr, in huwa illā dhikrul lil-ʿālamīn

ar: وَكَأَيِّن مِّنْ ءَايَةٍ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ
en: (105) And how many a sign within the heavens and earth do they pass over while they, therefrom, are turning away.
tr: Wakaʾayyim min āyatin fis-samāwāti wal-arḍi yamurrūna ʿalayhā wahum ʿanhā muʿriḍūn

ar: وَمَا يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُم بِٱللَّهِ إِلَّا وَهُم مُّشْرِكُونَ
en: (106) And most of them believe not in Allāh except while they associate others with Him.
tr: Wamā yuʾminu aktharuhum billāhi illā wahum mushrikūn

ar: أَفَأَمِنُوٓا۟ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ غَٰشِيَةٌ مِّنْ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
en: (107) Then do they feel secure that there will not come to them an overwhelming [aspect] of the punishment of Allāh or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?
tr: Afaʾaminū an taʾtiyahum ghāshiyatum min ʿadhābillāhi aw taʾtiyahumus-sāʿatu baghtataw wahum lā yashʿurūn

ar: قُلْ هَٰذِهِۦ سَبِيلِىٓ أَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا۠ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِى وَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ
en: (108) Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allāh with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allāh; and I am not of those who associate others with Him."
tr: Qul hādhihī sabīlī adʿū ilallāh, ʿalā baṣīratin ana wamanittabaʿanī, wasubḥānallāhi wamā ana minal-mushrikīn

ar: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِم مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ وَلَدَارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِّلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا۟ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
en: (109) And We sent not before you [as messengers] except men to whom We revealed from among the people of cities. So have they[620] not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allāh; then will you not reason?
enNotes: [620]- Those who deny Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).
tr: Wamā arsalnā min qablika illā rijālan nūḥī ilayhim min ahlil-qurā, afalam yasīrū fil-arḍi fayanẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatul-ladhīna min qablihim, waladārul-ākhirati khayrul lilladhīnattaqaw, afalā taʿqilūn

ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ٱسْتَيْـَٔسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا۟ جَآءَهُمْ نَصْرُنَا فَنُجِّىَ مَن نَّشَآءُ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنَا عَنِ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
en: (110) [They continued] until, when the messengers despaired and were certain that they had been denied, there came to them Our victory, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals.
tr: Ḥattā idhastayʾasar-rusulu waẓannū annahum qad kudhibū jāʾahum naṣrunā fanujjiya man nashāʾ, walā yuraddu baʾsunā ʿanil-qawmil-mujrimīn

ar: لَقَدْ كَانَ فِى قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ مَا كَانَ حَدِيثًا يُفْتَرَىٰ وَلَٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
en: (111) There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. Never was it [i.e., the Qur’ān] a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
tr: Laqad kāna fī qaṣaṣihim ʿibratul liʾulil-albāb, mā kāna ḥadīthay yuftarā walākin taṣdīqal-ladhī bayna yadayhi watafṣīla kulli shayʾiw wahudaw waraḥmatal liqawmiy yuʾminūn
